evidence.trustReason: Fresh-context Layer 3 review of packages/opencode/test/task/verify-spec-RM8c.spec.ts (committed b9553cc37d, unchanged); my own bare bun test run: 3 pass, 0 fail, 45 expect() calls. Reading of the Given, judged independently: the Gherkin header defines 'the observed facts' as run.started, T1.1-T1.3 trusted and T1.4's three failing builds, with no scenario facts. Taken literally, D3 and RM10 (the run settles only when every region is final) make that fold NOT done: S2, S3, S4, S7 and S12 (needs within T1.1-T1.3) stay pending, so the literal RM8c contradicts the binding decisions. The test states this openly: test 1 asserts the header facts alone fold to running with exactly those five scenarios pending and every other scenario blocked. It then stores the observed slice as the old engine wrote it. I verified this independently: base 2c0214ab71 core/runner.ts schedule proves every waiting scenario whose needs are all trusted, and release-notes T1.4 is after [T1.2, T1.3], so all five scenarios became provable before T1.4 started and were proved during its three builds. The stored slice equals the observed facts (asserted by shape) plus exactly those five scenarios' proofs and verdicts, run.started {base} with no path, no run.ended. So the Given is the real observed stored slice, not padding. When: TaskEvents.fold through the real engine. Then fold done, outcome budget exhausted, T1.5 and T1 blocked: status done, ended, no stored stop, run budget_exhausted with the exact reason lines, last history run running->budget_exhausted, T1.4 budget_exhausted, blockedBy {T1.4, budget_exhausted} for T1.5 and T1; one fact less is not done; a failed S3 and a rejected S4 give the same outcome. And /task starts a new slice, never resumes a done fold: sliceOf gives new for the stored slice and resume for one fact less (causal contrast); the real TaskCommand.run appends exactly {run.started, base, path: spec}, no run.resumed, two slices with the new one latest. Trusted on this reading. Spec-wording gap for the owner, not a test defect: the header definition of 'the observed facts' omits the scenario facts the old runner stored; the owner should reword the header or RM8c.
